build.prompt_version: Trump Diary Phase 1 Discovery Prompt v1

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Administrative state capture through DOGE, civil-service purge, and executive centralization
candidate_threads.description: A recurring project to subordinate the federal bureaucracy to presidential and Musk-aligned control through DOGE, mass firings, Schedule F-style politicization, agency hollowing, payment-system access, data consolidation, and the weakening of internal oversight and independent administration.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil service, oversight, and agencies are politicized and partially outsourced to Musk’s DOGE
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Introduces DOGE, Schedule F, targeted firings, and politicization of the machinery of government as a governing method.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump’s second inauguration unleashes a blitz of unilateral power grabs
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows the initial executive-centralization context in which agency subordination and oversight removal begin.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil service, oversight, and labor protections are gutted to build a loyalty-based state
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly centers stripping civil-service protections, watchdog purges, and political control over personnel data.

supporting_developments.development_title: Emergency powers and funding freezes test the limits of executive control over the purse
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Connects personnel capture to control over administrative spending flows.

supporting_developments.development_title: Musk’s DOGE apparatus and Trump loyalists capture the administrative state and federal payment infrastructure
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows DOGE access to Treasury, OPM, and regulatory agencies as a deepening administrative-state capture.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil service, USAID, and DEI structures are purged and reengineered around loyalty and exclusion
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds agency lockouts, workforce coercion, and replacement of neutral service norms with loyalty tests.

supporting_developments.development_title: DOGE becomes a parallel executive state and spearheads a civil service purge
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Depicts DOGE as an operational parallel state controlling hiring, firing, budgets, and sensitive systems.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil service, science, and education are hollowed out and ideologically reshaped
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the same pattern into science, education, and institutional capacity destruction.

supporting_developments.development_title: DOGE-Driven Purge Reshapes the Federal Workforce and Public Services
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows sustained, cross-agency layoffs and service degradation as a structural administrative method.

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive Power Sidesteps Congress and Courts to Centralize Control
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Reinforces that bureaucratic capture is part of a wider centralization project.

supporting_developments.development_title: Musk’s DOGE tightens control over federal money, data, and the civil service
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Further develops DOGE as fiscal and HR command center with control over payments, data, and agency personnel.

supporting_developments.development_title: The federal bureaucracy is hollowed out and repurposed toward loyalty and privatization
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows agency restructuring, layoffs, and service degradation as ongoing rather than one-off.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump centralizes power through sweeping executive orders and DOGE-driven state restructuring
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Continues the pattern of executive orders plus DOGE-led dismantling of agency capacity.

supporting_developments.development_title: DOGE’s austerity campaign and Musk’s messaging reshape the federal footprint while obscuring the true costs
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds the fiscal-cutting and narrative-management dimension of administrative contraction.

supporting_developments.development_title: Administrative state hollowed out and repurposed through DOGE, agency purges, and privatization
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Names the pattern directly and shows continuing agency capture, cuts, and reassignment of functions.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil service, unions, and core federal agencies come under structural attack
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows the same thread reaching major departments, unions, and core state capacity by week 10.

inclusion_notes: Include DOGE access to payment systems, personnel systems, and agency data.
Include mass layoffs, buyouts, probationary firings, agency dismantling, and workforce politicization.
Include weakening or removal of inspectors general, independent administrators, and neutral service protections when tied to executive control.
Include reassignment or closure of agency functions to make the bureaucracy more pliable or privately influenced.
exclusion_notes: Exclude standalone law-enforcement retaliation unless it primarily concerns bureaucratic capture.
Exclude general spending freezes when better understood as impoundment/power-of-the-purse conflict rather than state capture.
Exclude purely symbolic culture-war actions unless they are operationalized through agency restructuring.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_EXECUTIVE_OVERREACH_AND_IMPOUNDMENT, which focuses on separation-of-powers conflict over spending and unilateral authority rather than the bureaucracy’s internal capture.
Distinct from cand_CRONY_CAPITALISM_AND_PRIVATE_STATE_FUSION, which emphasizes enrichment and insider business advantage; overlap occurs when Musk’s private role and DOGE merge.
Overlaps with cand_INFO_CONTROL_AND_RECORD_ERASURE where data access or deletion is part of agency capture.
merge_suggestions: May merge with similarly named candidates about civil-service purge, DOGE capture, or bureaucratic politicization in other windows.
split_suggestions: Could later split DOGE/payment-system control from broader civil-service purge if year-wide material shows distinct trajectories.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Executive overreach through unilateral orders, impoundment, and defiance of institutional checks
candidate_threads.description: A recurring pattern in which the presidency claims authority to freeze or redirect funds, subordinate independent agencies, bypass Congress, and brush aside or test court limits, using emergency rhetoric and unilateral executive action to enlarge personal control over government.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump’s second inauguration unleashes a blitz of unilateral power grabs
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Establishes the opening pattern of emergency declarations, statute-defying moves, and subordinating independent agencies.

supporting_developments.development_title: Emergency powers and funding freezes test the limits of executive control over the purse
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly centers impoundment-like funding freezes and testing Congress’s control over appropriations.

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive power and foreign policy are radically centralized through aid freezes, tariffs, and multilateral withdrawals
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows unilateral use of tariffs, aid freezes, and foreign-policy tools without meaningful legislative constraint.

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive impoundment and fiscal brinkmanship weaponize the power of the purse
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Reinforces the power-of-the-purse conflict through freezes, seizures, debt threats, and court-ordered restorations.

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive Power Sidesteps Congress and Courts to Centralize Control
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Explicitly describes unilateral reinterpretation of statutes, White House control of independent agencies, and defiance of injunctions.

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive power defies oversight at home and reorients foreign policy abroad
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows pardons, funding freezes, court-defiance, and unilateral diplomacy as one executive-power thread.

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive power sidelines Congress on foreign aid, war powers, and legal accountability
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends unilateral control to arms transfers, aid impoundment, classified-document retrieval, and war powers.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump escalates a direct confrontation with the judiciary over deportations
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows unilateral executive claims escalating into open conflict with judicial authority over deportations.

inclusion_notes: Include freezes or redirections of congressionally appropriated money.
Include executive orders subordinating independent agencies or claiming emergency-style authority over routine governance.
Include overt defiance or narrowing of judicial orders when framed as presidential prerogative.
exclusion_notes: Exclude internal bureaucratic purge dynamics when the main issue is personnel capture rather than separation-of-powers conflict.
Exclude immigration-specific emergency powers when better captured under immigration-as-control unless the institutional conflict is central.
boundary_notes: Broader constitutional-overreach thread; many instances overlap with administrative capture but are not identical.
Overlaps with cand_JUDICIAL_INTIMIDATION_AND_RULE_OF_LAW_INVERSION when executive defiance turns into attacks on courts.
Foreign-policy unilateralism may later merge partly with a separate foreign-policy-personalization thread depending on wider-year evidence.
merge_suggestions: May merge with candidates labeled impoundment, emergency rule, or constitutional overreach.
split_suggestions: Could split domestic impoundment from foreign-policy unilateralism if later windows show clearer divergence.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Law as protection for allies and punishment for opponents, coupled with intimidation of courts and legal actors
candidate_threads.description: A recurring pattern in which pardons, dropped cases, prosecutorial intervention, retaliatory executive orders, and attacks on judges and law firms convert legal institutions from neutral constraints into tools that protect regime allies and punish opponents or investigators.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil rights enforcement is frozen while law is bent to protect regime-aligned causes
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Sets the initial pattern of pardons, selective non-enforcement, and protection for aligned offenders.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump weaponizes law and pardons to erase January 6 accountability and shield himself
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly centers pardons, personnel purges, and record deletion as a shield for Trump and allies.

supporting_developments.development_title: Justice Department, FBI, and oversight mechanisms are purged and repurposed to shield Trump and allies
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows DOJ/FBI repurposing, Jan. 6 pardons, and dismantling of oversight as a coherent legal inversion.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law enforcement and justice are repurposed to shield allies and target enemies
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Ties anti-corruption pauses, political intervention, and judge intimidation into one rule-of-law inversion pattern.

supporting_developments.development_title: Justice System Bent Toward Regime Protection and Impunity for Allies
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Continues prosecutorial coercion, purges, pardons, and selective enforcement against disfavored groups.

supporting_developments.development_title: Judicial independence and legal oversight face intimidation, but courts still check some abuses
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows impeachment threats against judges, targeting of legal adversaries, and pressure on courts as the next-stage escalation.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump escalates a direct confrontation with the judiciary over deportations
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds personal attacks, impeachment pushes, and narrowing claims against judges overseeing executive misconduct.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law becomes a weapon: Trump targets disfavored law firms, judges, and civil servants
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the pattern to executive orders against law firms, politicized appointments, and punishments based on loyalty.

aliases: attack on law firms and judges
inclusion_notes: Include pardons, dropped cases, coercive prosecutorial interventions, and dismantling of anti-corruption enforcement.
Include impeachment threats, public smears, or executive retaliation aimed at judges or law firms.
Include selective use of law enforcement to protect allies while burdening critics or opponents.
exclusion_notes: Exclude generic court losses or lawsuits unless the response involves intimidation or inversion of legal neutrality.
Exclude bureaucratic purges unless they directly concern justice institutions or legal accountability.
boundary_notes: Adjacent to cand_ADMIN_STATE_CAPTURE_AND_DOGE but centered on legal institutions, not the bureaucracy generally.
Adjacent to cand_INFO_CONTROL_AND_RECORD_ERASURE where records deletion serves impunity; the core here is legal protection and coercion.
Immigration-specific uses of law belong with cand_IMMIGRATION_AND_CITIZENSHIP_AS_CONTROL unless the main point is court intimidation or selective legality.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with year-wide candidates around 'law as protection for allies and punishment for enemies' or DOJ politicization.
split_suggestions: Could split judicial intimidation from prosecutorial/legal impunity if later windows support two durable subthreads.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Immigration, asylum, and citizenship used as instruments of tiered belonging and dissent control
candidate_threads.description: A sustained pattern of recasting immigration, asylum, and citizenship as emergency-security tools to stratify rights, expand detention and deportation, challenge birthright citizenship, and use status vulnerability to discipline migrants, students, activists, and disfavored communities.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration, citizenship, and the border are recast as a permanent emergency
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Introduces the emergency framing, deportation expansion, asylum suspension, and birthright citizenship challenge.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration, citizenship, and protest rights are recast through mass raids and tiered status
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows raids, Guantánamo expansion, TPS changes, and ties between status and protest suppression.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration, asylum, and citizenship are restructured through hardline executive orders and offshored detention
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds asylum suspension, offshore detention, birthright attack, and legal uncertainty as instruments of control.

supporting_developments.development_title: Citizenship and public health are redefined along ideological and identity lines
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the thread into selective asylum, anti-trans and vaccine-linked public policy, and identity-based access to protections.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration and Citizenship Policy Harden Into a Tiered System of Rights
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows benefit cuts, status threats, courthouse arrests, and immigration precarity as a durable governance method.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump accelerates mass deportation and a tiered immigration regime
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Combines deportation escalation, biometric registration, Guantánamo use, and purchasable citizenship.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration and citizenship policy harden into a tiered system of rights
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Continues mass deportation plans, family detention, travel bans, English-only policy, and nationality-based hierarchy.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration and citizenship are weaponized into a multi-tier system of belonging
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows birthright citizenship attack, family detention, offshore detention, and status revocations for activists and families.

supporting_developments.development_title: Alien Enemies Act mass deportations defy courts and normalize emergency rule
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Escalates the thread into wartime-style deportation powers and court-defying removals.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration powers weaponized against activists, academics, and stratified citizenship
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Highlights targeting of activists and academics through immigration status and detention powers.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration and citizenship tools are weaponized against dissenters and marginalized groups
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows continued use of visa controls, deportation powers, and data-sharing against protesters, students, and migrants.

inclusion_notes: Include asylum suspension, mass deportation, detention expansion, Guantánamo/offshore detention, biometric registration, and birthright citizenship attacks.
Include use of immigration status to discipline activists, students, campus protest, or ideological enemies.
Include policies that create differentiated membership based on nationality, wealth, race, or political behavior.
exclusion_notes: Exclude generic foreign-policy immigration disputes unless they materially alter domestic belonging or enforcement.
Exclude broader civil-rights rollbacks not tied to immigration status or citizenship.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_CAMPUS_AND_DISSENT_SUPPRESSION, though campus repression often uses immigration tools.
Distinct from cand_JUDICIAL_INTIMIDATION_AND_RULE_OF_LAW_INVERSION; court conflict around deportations belongs here only when the core pattern is status-based control.
Some public-health and identity-based exclusions overlap with cand_HIERARCHICAL_CITIZENSHIP_AND_ANTI_EQUALITY_ORDER.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with year-wide candidates on immigration as control, stratified citizenship, or border emergency rule.
split_suggestions: Could later split general mass-deportation regime from activist/student targeting if both recur strongly across later windows.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Rights, recognition, and public belonging reordered along lines of gender, race, religion, and ideology
candidate_threads.description: A recurring campaign to dismantle DEI, target transgender people, narrow reproductive and civil-rights protections, elevate favored religious/national identities, and re-sort who receives recognition, safety, or equal treatment in public institutions.

supporting_developments.development_title: DEI, gender, and reproductive rights are rolled back to enforce a narrower social order
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Sets the baseline pattern of DEI dismantling, anti-trans policy, abortion funding restrictions, and Christian favoritism.

supporting_developments.development_title: DEI, LGBTQ+ rights, and civic education are dismantled across government, schools, and prisons
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the rollback across schools, prisons, military, and federal agencies.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil and human rights are rolled back along lines of gender, race, religion, and punishment
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows anti-trans, anti-civil-rights, anti-protest, and punitive measures as one hierarchy-building project.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil service, USAID, and DEI structures are purged and reengineered around loyalty and exclusion
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds the institutional purge dimension tied to exclusionary norms.

supporting_developments.development_title: Citizenship and public health are redefined along ideological and identity lines
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Demonstrates identity-based sorting in asylum, trans rights, and public-health access.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civic Education, Culture, and Public Memory Are Rewritten Along Ideological Lines
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows equality rollback extending into cultural recognition and curriculum.

supporting_developments.development_title: Coordinated assault on transgender people and DEI across government, schools, and culture
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: A clear continuation of anti-trans targeting plus anti-DEI infrastructure removal.

supporting_developments.development_title: Coordinated attacks on LGBTQ rights, reproductive autonomy, and DEI reshape civil equality
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds state and federal coordination on trans rights, abortion access, and anti-DEI enforcement.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil rights, labor protections, and diversity infrastructure are rolled back across the state
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the thread into formal civil-rights enforcement rollback and diversity-program termination.

supporting_developments.development_title: Rights and policing: selective protections amid ongoing abuses and activism
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows ongoing contest over whose rights are protected, including anti-DEI pressure and trans-related state coercion.

inclusion_notes: Include anti-DEI orders, anti-trans policies, abortion/reproductive restrictions, and privileging of favored religious or nationalist identities.
Include agency or school policies that erase equality infrastructure or reduce formal protection for marginalized groups.
Include identity-based public-health or institutional access restrictions when part of a hierarchy-building project.
exclusion_notes: Exclude immigration-status hierarchy when migration control is the main engine; those belong in cand_IMMIGRATION_AND_CITIZENSHIP_AS_CONTROL.
Exclude memory/education erasure when the main issue is narrative control rather than unequal rights.
boundary_notes: This is a rights-order thread, not just a culture-war topic.
Overlaps with cand_INFO_CONTROL_AND_RECORD_ERASURE when erasure of marginalized histories supports unequal citizenship.
May later need splitting between anti-trans/sexual-gender hierarchy and broader anti-DEI/civil-rights rollback if evidence strengthens.
merge_suggestions: May merge with year-wide candidates on anti-DEI rollback, gender hierarchy, or selective civil-rights enforcement.
split_suggestions: Potential future split between anti-trans governance and broader anti-DEI/civil-rights dismantling.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Information control, record erasure, and narrative management
candidate_threads.description: A recurring pattern of scrubbing public data, deleting records, restricting media access, reshaping archives and history, manipulating official language, and flooding the public sphere with regime-favoring narratives while making scrutiny harder.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information control and propaganda reshape what the public can see and believe
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Introduces gag orders, transparency rollback, symbolic renaming, and pressure on media.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information, archives, and symbolism are curated to erase inconvenient realities and glorify the regime
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Centers deletion of archives, symbolic rewrites, and curated public memory.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information, media access, and public memory are systematically manipulated to favor the regime
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds data removal, media access restructuring, and private-platform/state fusion.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information, memory, and culture are aggressively rewritten to fit regime narratives
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows state-curated reality through site scrubbing, archive purges, and retaliatory media restrictions.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information Control Tightens: Media Punished, Data Seized, and Critics Cast as Threats
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds media punishment, data grabs, and criminalizing criticism.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civic Education, Culture, and Public Memory Are Rewritten Along Ideological Lines
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows narrative control extending into schools, symbols, and historical memory.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information space and culture brought under tighter political control
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Continues language control, media access restrictions, propaganda ecosystems, and cultural pressure.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information control, propaganda, and curated memory tighten around the regime’s narratives
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Reinforces propaganda, archive control, naming disputes, and data manipulation.

supporting_developments.development_title: Media, information, and archives come under coordinated pressure at home and abroad
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Centers media defunding, records destruction, scientific-information suppression, and transparency fights.

supporting_developments.development_title: Media, information, and history are reshaped to favor regime narratives
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows AP access restrictions, USAGM/VOA dismantling, content deletions, and propaganda repurposing.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information control, media attacks, and the fight over national memory intensify
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the thread into museum control, banned words, media attacks, and educational memory battles.

inclusion_notes: Include deletion or alteration of government websites, databases, advisories, and historical content.
Include restrictions on media access or pressure on outlets over language or criticism.
Include archive purges, museum/history interventions, and propagandistic symbolic renaming when part of public-memory control.
exclusion_notes: Exclude ordinary misinformation unless tied to institutional efforts to control records, access, or public knowledge.
Exclude surveillance/data access focused mainly on bureaucratic control unless public-information consequences are central.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_ADMIN_STATE_CAPTURE_AND_DOGE: the latter is about controlling the bureaucracy; this thread is about controlling what the public can know.
Distinct from cand_CAMPUS_AND_DISSENT_SUPPRESSION: campus cases belong there when coercion of protest is primary rather than information shaping.
Often supports and amplifies nearly every other thread by reducing accountability visibility.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with year-wide candidates on information control, archive erasure, or propaganda-state tactics.
split_suggestions: Could later split media access/punishment from historical-memory rewriting if both become independently robust.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Crony capitalism and private-state fusion around Trump, Musk, and allied insiders
candidate_threads.description: A recurring pattern in which public power, regulation, contracts, tariffs, sovereign or crypto initiatives, and enforcement decisions are steered toward the financial interests of Trump, Musk, family members, donors, and aligned firms, blurring the line between state action and private enrichment.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony capitalism and personal enrichment are woven into core economic policy
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Introduces sovereign wealth, crypto, family deals, and public policy aligned with insider profit.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony capitalism and billionaire influence blur the line between public office and private gain
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows presidential ventures, Musk’s systems role, and settlements/regulatory choices favoring insiders.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony capitalism and Trump family ventures intertwine with state power
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Links family ventures and state tools in finance, diplomacy, and regulation.

supporting_developments.development_title: Musk’s DOGE apparatus and Trump loyalists capture the administrative state and federal payment infrastructure
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows private influence over state infrastructure as the enabling mechanism of private-state fusion.

supporting_developments.development_title: Austerity and Fossil-Fuel Policy Shift Economic Burdens Onto the Vulnerable
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows economic policy redistributing burdens downward while favoring aligned industries and narratives of fraud.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law and regulation bent to favor donors and regime‑aligned business
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly centers favorable treatment for donors, crypto firms, and insider ventures.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony capitalism and the crypto reserve blur the line between public policy and private enrichment
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the thread into federal crypto reserve policy and donor-linked selective non-enforcement.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony capitalism and Musk’s expanding role blur lines between public power and private profit
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows contract shifts, state support for Musk-linked firms, and security rhetoric protecting private assets.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony capitalism and personal enrichment fuse with federal policy
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Continues with meme coin promotion, tariffs, pardons, sponsorships, and protection of favored firms.

inclusion_notes: Include policy, contract, regulatory, clemency, or enforcement decisions that materially advantage Trump, Musk, family members, donors, or aligned firms.
Include crypto reserve or meme-coin governance, favored contracting, tariff favoritism, and explicit monetization of office.
Include use of security or state messaging to defend allied firms when tied to insider advantage.
exclusion_notes: Exclude general neoliberal or deregulatory policy unless the insider-benefit pattern is clear.
Exclude DOGE staffing/control issues when no private enrichment or business advantage is evident.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_ADMIN_STATE_CAPTURE_AND_DOGE, though DOGE often provides the mechanism for this thread.
Distinct from cand_EXECUTIVE_OVERREACH_AND_IMPOUNDMENT; the constitutional issue may overlap, but this thread is about who profits.
May eventually require a Musk-specific subthread if later windows show a uniquely durable pattern around federal IT/contracts/security rhetoric.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with candidates labeled private-state fusion, crony capitalism, oligarchic capture, or personal enrichment.
split_suggestions: Possible future split between Trump-family enrichment and Musk-centered state fusion.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Campuses, protest, and civil dissent targeted through funding, surveillance, and punitive enforcement
candidate_threads.description: A recurring pattern of using university funding threats, antisemitism or security investigations, visa/deportation powers, police and administrative discipline, and public rhetoric to suppress student protest, academic freedom, and broader dissent—especially pro-Palestinian activism.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration, citizenship, and protest rights are recast through mass raids and tiered status
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Early evidence that protest rights and immigration/status tools are being linked in enforcement logic.

supporting_developments.development_title: Universities and campuses become battlegrounds for speech control and punishment
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly frames universities as sites of funding threats, investigations, and ideological discipline.

supporting_developments.development_title: Universities and campuses are pressured to police pro-Palestinian dissent under threat of federal punishment
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows explicit federal coercion of campus protest handling through grants, visa actions, and discipline.

supporting_developments.development_title: Universities and education policy become battlegrounds for suppressing dissent and reshaping civic life
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds coercive funding freezes, education restructuring, and protest-related ideological compliance demands.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration and citizenship tools are weaponized against dissenters and marginalized groups
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Continues use of visa controls, detentions, and data-sharing against students, academics, and protesters.

inclusion_notes: Include federal funding threats or cuts tied to protest handling or ideological compliance on campus.
Include visa revocations, immigration detention, or security investigations directed at students, faculty, or academic speech.
Include coercive campus discipline when driven by federal pressure or linked to national dissent control.
exclusion_notes: Exclude general anti-DEI school policy unless protest suppression or ideological discipline of dissent is central.
Exclude broad education-agency dismantling unless directly tied to campus speech or protest control.
boundary_notes: This is narrower than general civil-rights rollback and narrower than immigration-as-control; it preserves the specific university/protest mechanism.
Strong overlap with cand_IMMIGRATION_AND_CITIZENSHIP_AS_CONTROL because immigration law is often the tool used against campus dissent.
Strong overlap with cand_INFO_CONTROL_AND_RECORD_ERASURE where campus narratives are policed, but here the coercive punishment dimension is primary.
merge_suggestions: May merge with future candidates about protest suppression or academic-freedom repression if they recur outside campuses.
split_suggestions: Could later expand into a broader dissent-suppression thread if non-campus protest control becomes more central.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Reactive resistance by courts, states, unions, and civil society
candidate_threads.description: A recurring counter-thread in which judges, state governments, unions, professional associations, media plaintiffs, and grassroots movements file suits, issue injunctions, organize protests, and attempt to slow or partially reverse executive overreach and institutional capture.

supporting_developments.development_title: States, courts, and civil society mount early resistance to Trump’s agenda
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Introduces the reactive pattern of lawsuits, union action, state countermeasures, and civic organizing.

Campus repression emerges more clearly from weeks 7-10 and may or may not warrant stand-alone status year-wide depending on later windows.

notes_on_window: The clearest sustained threads across weeks 5-14 are administrative-state capture, executive overreach, immigration as a control system, and information/memory control.
Several themes intensify in the back half of the window, especially voting-rule restriction and coercion of universities/law firms/civil society.
Cronyism/private-state fusion is visible but somewhat less uniformly foregrounded than the core state-capture and immigration threads.
Court resistance appears often, but mostly as context or counterpressure rather than as a standalone continuity thread for catalogue purposes.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.label: Fragmented resistance
rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Visible in several weeks but functions mostly as a cross-cutting counterforce rather than a governing method of democratic erosion; better treated as context in later phases.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.label: Emergency tariff regime
rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Too narrow as a standalone year-level thread within this window; better treated as a manifestation of executive overreach and, secondarily, crony economic governance.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.label: Signal scandal / off-channel national security communications
rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Important recurring scandal pattern but not broad enough in this window to stand as a main continuity thread apart from information control and executive unaccountability.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.label: Third-term and personal-rule norm testing
rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Meaningful but too intermittently visible in this window to justify separate thread status; folded into broader executive-power expansion and personalized rule.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.label: Environmental deregulation and fossil-fuel favoritism
rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Recurs, but within this window it reads more as a policy theater nested inside executive emergency rule, administrative capture, and crony extraction than as a distinct continuity thread.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.label: Courts as partial resistance
rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Appears frequently, but as an institutional response pattern rather than a primary erosion method; better preserved contextually within supporting developments and boundary notes.

notes_on_window: This window shows several clearly sustained threads rather than one-off topics: immigration as a control system, administrative-state capture, information control, private-state fusion, and weaponized law are visible across most of the ten weeks.
Election-rule manipulation is strong in weeks 10-13 but less visible later in the window, so it is treated as a recurring thread rather than sustained across the full span.

A number of weekly developments combine adjacent mechanisms (for example, campus coercion through both immigration tools and funding threats); boundary notes aim to preserve later merge flexibility rather than force premature exclusivity.
Court resistance appears frequently but mainly as a countervailing context inside stronger substantive threads, except where executive defiance of courts itself is the recurring pattern.

notes_on_window: This window shows especially strong continuity around immigration as an authoritarian testbed, with repeated overlap between deportation, detention, due-process denial, and dissent control.
Information control appears in two distinct but connected modes: direct media/public-broadcaster pressure and broader rewriting of education, memory, and symbolic history.
Universities are persistent targets across the window and are important enough to preserve separately from the broader information-control thread.
Administrative state capture and crony capitalism are both strong; they overlap often but remain analytically distinct in this window.
Several weekly allocator packages include explicit 'resistance' developments, but these work better here as contextual support or boundary markers than as primary continuity threads.

notes_on_window: Window 17-26 shows especially strong continuity in immigration/status coercion, information control, executive maximalism, and linked civil-service/fiscal restructuring.
Several weekly developments frame immigration as both a legal-status hierarchy and a militarized enforcement system; both threads are visible and worth preserving separately for later consolidation.

Harvard/university retaliation appears often enough to preserve as a sub-thread, but it may later fold into a broader knowledge-institutions or immigration-as-control thread depending on other windows.
Foreign-policy war powers appear clearly in weeks 23 and 25, but within this window they are better treated as a component of executive maximalism than as a standalone thread.

Civil-society resistance recurs, especially in weeks 19, 21, 22, and 26, but in this window it reads more as a countercurrent than a governing continuity thread on the same level as the coercive patterns.

notes_on_window: This window strongly supports several sustained recurring threads rather than mostly emergent ones; immigration-as-control, information control, and crony economic rule are especially visible across many consecutive weeks.

A major boundary issue is separating broad executive-overreach patterns from narrower mechanism threads like administrative-state capture or weaponized law; both are retained because the window repeatedly supplies evidence for each.
Immigration-related material is dense enough to support both an enforcement-apparatus thread and a broader stratified-citizenship thread; they should not be collapsed automatically.
Information-control material is also dense enough for a super-thread with sub-threads on media/archives and science/education/data capture.
Some week packages foreground resistance/countercurrents, but these are better treated as contextual evidence within major threads than as a standalone candidate continuity thread for this window.

notes_on_window: The window shows unusually strong continuity around immigration enforcement as both a carceral apparatus and a broader theory of tiered belonging.
A later-window escalation is visible around domestic militarization and city-directed emergency governance, especially from weeks 30-34.
Information control is sustained across the entire window but changes form: from public media/data manipulation to archives, museums, AI propaganda, and scandal secrecy.
Election-engineering becomes more explicit and structural in the back half of the window, especially through redistricting, mail-voting attacks, and national voter-data ambitions.

Some week-specific developments on foreign policy alignment with Russia or on public health misinformation were important but less consistently present across the full 10-week window than the chosen core threads.

notes_on_window: Window 009 shows especially strong continuity around immigration as a domestic-security regime, law as asymmetric punishment/protection, information control, and late-window shutdown coercion.
Several week-level developments combine multiple mechanisms; candidate threads here separate recurring methods from one-off headline events.
The shutdown pattern becomes clearly visible only in the later half of the window, so it is treated as a strong window-local thread rather than assumed year-wide dominance.
Chicago, Portland, DC, and other cities often function as test sites for broader threads rather than separate candidate threads.
Some identity-and-belonging material is embedded inside immigration, housing, passport, and social-policy stories; a narrower stratified-belonging thread is preserved but may later merge upward.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump escalates direct attacks on political opponents, media, and protest as "terrorism"
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Contains direct calls for arrest and the branding of opposition as terrorists or anti-American.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump escalates eliminationist rhetoric and coercion against lawmakers, media, and dissenters
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Most explicit example of death-threat rhetoric, treason framing, and regulatory intimidation.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump escalates use of law and security apparatus against political opponents
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows rhetoric translating into investigative and legal follow-through against opponents.

aliases: calls for arrest or execution of opponents
inclusion_notes: Include explicit threats of arrest, execution, treason treatment, or disqualification directed at named opponents or dissenting groups.
Include cases where rhetoric is closely coupled to institutional follow-through.
exclusion_notes: Exclude ordinary partisan insults or generic protest delegitimization unless punitive threat language is clear.
Exclude broader lawfare absent direct threat rhetoric.
boundary_notes: Best treated as narrower than cand_LAW_AS_WEAPON_AND_IMPUNITY and cand_SECURITY_FORCES_AGAINST_DISSENT: this thread is about the rhetoric of political annihilation itself.
May fold into a larger 'criminalization of opposition' thread during consolidation if later windows do not sustain distinct usefulness.
merge_suggestions: Possible fold into 'criminalization of opposition' or broader lawfare/repression thread if later windows do not preserve a separate rhetorical pattern.

notes_on_window: Window 37-46 shows especially strong continuity around immigration as domestic control, weaponized law/impunity, information control, and administrative-state capture.
The shutdown is clearly a major recurring method in weeks 37-43, then recedes; it is best kept as a distinct window-visible thread rather than stretched beyond its evidence.
Several developments show strong overlap between immigration control and domestic militarization; boundary notes preserve the distinction between status-based hierarchy and force-based repression.
Anti-trans and broader identity-targeting become especially visible later in the window and may be emergent rather than fully sustained in this slice alone.
Cronyism/private-state fusion is visible across economic, foreign-policy, and pardon/contract stories, suggesting a durable cross-domain pattern.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.label: Chicago as authoritarian laboratory
rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Important recurring case study in early weeks but better treated as a local manifestation of immigration-as-control and security-forces-against-dissent rather than a year-level thread.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.label: Epstein files transparency fight
rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Visible in multiple later weeks, but within this window it functions mostly as a subcase of weaponized law/impunity and information control rather than a standalone governing method.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.label: Resistance by courts, governors, and civil society
rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Recurring but primarily a countervailing response category rather than an authoritarian continuity thread or method of erosion.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.label: Tariff pain and economic mismanagement
rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Too topic-like on its own in this window; strongest continuity comes when folded into crony capitalism/private-state fusion or shutdown weaponization.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.label: Culture-war governance
rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Too broad and generic; sharper continuity is captured by stratified rights/identity targeting and information/memory control.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Immigration and citizenship powers used as tools of domestic control and tiered belonging
candidate_threads.description: A sustained pattern in which immigration enforcement, detention, asylum restrictions, denaturalization threats, nationality-targeted measures, and militarized raids are used not simply for border administration but to discipline communities, stratify rights, and extend coercive state power inward.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration and security apparatus repurposed for domestic control and political targeting
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly frames immigration and security institutions as instruments of domestic control, political targeting, concealed detention, and ideological sorting.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration enforcement hardens into a militarized, privatized detention regime
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows raids, privatized detention, surveillance infrastructure, and expanded confinement as a continuing governing method.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration enforcement escalates into a rights crisis, met by scattered judicial pushback
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the pattern through biometric tracking, mass raids, abusive arrests, Venezuelan transfers, and court efforts to slow the enforcement surge.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration and foreign policy tools used to punish dissent and project hard power abroad
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds the use of visa revocation and detention against a critic, showing immigration tools applied to speech and dissent.

supporting_developments.development_title: Operation Charlotte’s Web and National Guard deployments turn immigration enforcement into a domestic security campaign
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows interior raids paired with Guard deployments and federal pressure on localities, deepening the domestic-security dimension of immigration enforcement.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration and citizenship become central tools of social control
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Explicitly ties status reviews, denaturalization threats, family detention, and wrongful detention of citizens or residents to a system of social control.

supporting_developments.development_title: Security forces and quasi-paramilitary tactics are turned inward to intimidate communities and lawmakers
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Highlights masked street snatches, raids, and intimidation effects that overlap with the immigration-control apparatus.

supporting_developments.development_title: From rhetoric to regime: a racialized immigration crackdown and tiered citizenship
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds blanket asylum pauses, nationality-based reviews, travel bans, database integration, and dehumanizing rhetoric as tools of a tiered polity.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration enforcement hardens into a militarized, two-tier system
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Synthesizes policy design, deportation infrastructure, military zones, community-specific crackdowns, and status stratification.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration enforcement hardens into a racialized, quasi-military regime
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows Supreme Court-enabled profiling, raids reaching citizens and children, and local/court pushback against quasi-military enforcement.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigrant scapegoating and anti-dissent narratives are amplified through official propaganda and policing
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds the propaganda layer that legitimizes aggressive immigration policing and stigmatizes targeted communities.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration Enforcement Expands into a Militarized, Dehumanizing Apparatus
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows major funding buildout, warehouse detention, foreign-prison deportations, and celebratory/dehumanizing official tone.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration enforcement is industrialized and personalized under Trump
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Carries the thread into denaturalization quotas, country-based freezes, warehouse detention, recruitment surges, and direct presidential personalization of control.

aliases: immigration and citizenship as tools of social control
two-tier system for immigrants and citizens
inclusion_notes: Include raids, detention expansion, deportation logistics, asylum freezes, travel bans, denaturalization threats, citizenship/status reviews, and the use of immigration tools against critics or communities.
Include policy architecture plus on-the-ground enforcement and its carceral or military features.
Include official rhetoric when it directly supports coercive immigration governance.
exclusion_notes: Do not fold all protest-policing or war powers here unless immigration enforcement is central.
Do not treat every foreign-policy action involving migration as part of this thread unless it clearly affects domestic control, belonging, or deportation governance.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_SECURITY_POWERS_AND_MILITARIZED_GOVERNANCE, which covers broader war powers, Guard deployments, and national-security framing beyond immigration.
Distinct from cand_INFO_CONTROL_AND_PROPAGANDA, which covers narrative management; propaganda belongs here only when directly enabling immigration coercion.
Related to cand_STRATIFIED_RIGHTS_AND_EXCLUSIONARY_IDENTITY_RULE but narrower and more institutionally centered on immigration/citizenship machinery.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with parallel window labels about deportation regime, tiered citizenship, or immigration as social control.
Possible future split between enforcement infrastructure and citizenship-status stratification if year-wide evidence supports both.
split_suggestions: Could split off a sub-thread focused specifically on denaturalization, citizenship revocation, and nationality-tiering if later windows show sustained distinct continuity.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Law used to protect allies, punish opponents, and manage elite accountability
candidate_threads.description: A recurring thread in which prosecutions, pardons, secrecy claims, selective investigations, procedural abuses, and clemency are used asymmetrically—shielding Trump-aligned actors and elites while targeting rivals, critics, or inconvenient accountability efforts.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law enforcement and courts increasingly weaponized against critics as Trump seeks personal legal revenge
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly establishes prosecutions, claims, record demands, and media pressure as instruments of Trump’s personal legal revenge.

supporting_developments.development_title: Pardons, politicized justice, and the burial of elite wrongdoing
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Centers pardons, selective DOJ behavior, and obscuring elite wrongdoing as a core governing pattern.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law and justice bent toward Trump’s interests: pardons, politicized probes, and elite impunity
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows clemency, politicized probes, and shielding of insiders as a coherent legal-order distortion.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law as weapon: Epstein files, targeted investigations, and elite impunity
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Combines transparency fights, targeted investigations, secrecy claims, and elite-friendly justice in one recurring arc.

supporting_developments.development_title: Trump escalates use of law and security apparatus against political opponents
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the pattern through investigations of lawmakers and impunity for pro-Trump election offenders.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law and clemency repurposed to shield corrupt elites and rewrite legal continuity
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows high-profile pardons and attacks on legal continuity as means of ally protection and retaliatory governance.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil and criminal accountability for past abuses advances unevenly through the Epstein files and January 6 cases
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds the accountability side of the same struggle, showing elite abuse and political-violence cases moving unevenly under pressure.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law and justice are weaponized to shield allies, punish critics, and test judicial independence
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Reinforces the asymmetry of pardons, selective prosecution, removal power fights, and gerrymander-related legal manipulation.

supporting_developments.development_title: Epstein files confrontation exposes deepening impunity and archival manipulation
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows legal noncompliance and archival curation serving elite protection.

supporting_developments.development_title: Epstein Files Transparency Mandate Collides with a Defiant, Politicized DOJ
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Highlights DOJ noncompliance and curation in a major elite-accountability case.

supporting_developments.development_title: Rule of Law Distorted: Selective Enforcement, Conflicts of Interest, and Targeting of Rivals
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Explicitly captures selective enforcement, conflicts of interest, and rhetorical targeting of opponents.

supporting_developments.development_title: Epstein revelations and elite accountability battles expose a two-tier justice system
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows the two-tier treatment of elite-linked crimes versus aggressive enforcement elsewhere.

inclusion_notes: Include prosecutions or investigations aimed at rivals, pardons or clemency for allies, procedural abuse, secrecy maneuvers, conflicts of interest in DOJ activity, and management of elite-accountability cases.
Include major accountability fights over Epstein and similar elite-abuse records when the emphasis is on legal shielding, curation, or noncompliance.
exclusion_notes: Do not include generic court pushback unless it is part of the same ally-protection/opponent-punishment dynamic.
Do not collapse agency capture or civil-service politicization into this thread unless legal tools are the main mechanism.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_ADMINISTRATIVE_STATE_CAPTURE, which centers agency restructuring and bureaucratic control rather than prosecutorial asymmetry.
Distinct from cand_INFO_CONTROL_AND_PROPAGANDA, though secrecy and curation around legal records often overlap.
Related to cand_EPSILON_ELITE_ACCOUNTABILITY_AND_EPSTEIN_FILES as a likely sub-thread if later consolidation preserves Epstein-specific continuity.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with window-level labels around weaponized DOJ, politicized justice, clemency abuse, or two-tier justice.
Epstein-specific candidates may fold into this thread or survive as a child thread depending on cross-window density.
split_suggestions: Could split into sub-threads for 'clemency and ally protection' and 'targeted investigations of enemies' if later windows show cleaner separation.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Information control, propaganda, and public-memory management
candidate_threads.description: A sustained pattern of controlling public narratives through censorship pressure, official disinformation, record curation, attacks on media, manipulation of science and statistics, symbolic memory politics, and deliberate flooding of the public sphere with regime-serving narratives.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information space and civic memory reshaped through propaganda, censorship, and chaos
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly frames partisan websites, falsehoods, censorship, and chaos as methods of information control.

supporting_developments.development_title: Knowledge and culture under pressure: universities, media, and identity narratives
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds pressure on universities and media as institutions that shape public knowledge and acceptable narratives.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information warfare and AI‑driven disinformation reshape elections and protest narratives
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows AI-driven spectacle, misinformation laundering, and narrative distortion in politics and protest coverage.

supporting_developments.development_title: Struggle over Epstein files and elite accountability collides with efforts to curate public memory
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Connects transparency fights to executive efforts to curate museum content and historical narrative.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information and memory are curated by power—from trans erasure to media pressure and Chinese controls
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Provides a clear expression of data erasure, media intimidation, and curated memory as a governing strategy.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information, media, and memory are aggressively curated to favor the regime
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows canceled data, rewritten science, broadcaster threats, book purges, and politicized commemorative messaging.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information warfare, managed opacity, and the curation of memory
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds official targeting of media, suppression of indicators, and politicized science under a managed-opacity frame.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information systems and media are retooled for propaganda, speculation, and leader-centric branding
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the thread into media-market manipulation, bias-reporting channels, leader branding, and data/communication control.

supporting_developments.development_title: Memory, media, and cultural institutions are reshaped to glorify Trump and mute scrutiny
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows cultural institutions, regulator alignment, lawsuits, and third-term signaling being used to remake memory and scrutiny.

supporting_developments.development_title: Media Intimidation, Self-Censorship, and the Weaponization of Official Communications
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly ties journalist violence, self-censorship, official smears, and conspiratorial messaging into one information-control arc.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information control, disinformation, and the Epstein files fight reshape what the public is allowed to know
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Captures censorship, punishment of anti-disinformation actors, propaganda, and slow-walked disclosure of politically sensitive records.

inclusion_notes: Include attacks on media, government disinformation, suppression or manipulation of data/science, symbolic memory politics, official propaganda sites, and archive curation.
Include cultural-institution capture when it primarily affects what the public can know, remember, or publicly say.
exclusion_notes: Do not include every legal secrecy dispute unless narrative control or archival curation is central.
Do not fold all education culture-war content here when the main mechanism is rights stratification rather than information control.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_RULE_BY_LAW_AND_ALLY_IMPUNITY, though Epstein-file curation and legal secrecy often overlap.
Distinct from cand_ADMINISTRATIVE_STATE_CAPTURE, though politicization of science agencies can support both.
Related to cand_PERSONALIST_STATE_AND_SYMBOLIC_DOMINANCE where branding and glorification are directed at Trump personally.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with labels around propaganda, media intimidation, record erasure, memory politics, or disinformation governance.
Could absorb some science-politicization candidates depending on later-window overlap.
split_suggestions: Potential split between 'media intimidation/disinformation' and 'memory/archives/cultural institutions' if later consolidation needs finer resolution.

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive power expands into war and nuclear policy with scant oversight and a partisan military edge
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Establishes unilateral nuclear and military actions, partisan military rhetoric, and weak oversight as an early form of the thread.

supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows a broad theory of near-unchecked presidential force at home and abroad, with Congress bypassed.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration and foreign policy tools used to punish dissent and project hard power abroad
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds military deployments and transactional use of hard power, though mixed with dissent-punishment logic.

supporting_developments.development_title: Operation Charlotte’s Web and National Guard deployments turn immigration enforcement into a domestic security campaign
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows domestic federal deployments and security-force use in cities, overlapping with militarized governance.

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive power stretches past traditional limits through sweeping orders and emergency claims
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds emergency rationales and war-powers creep as instruments of unilateral control.

supporting_developments.development_title: Security forces and war powers stretched toward extrajudicial violence and regime protection
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Centers lethal maritime strikes, politicized policing, and security institutions bent toward regime protection.

supporting_developments.development_title: Protest and dissent squeezed by immigration crackdowns, policing tactics, and targeted investigations
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows policing and protest suppression as the domestic-facing edge of the same security-state expansion.

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive power and security forces stretch beyond traditional oversight at home and abroad
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly links Caribbean strikes, Guard moves, police federalization, and weak oversight.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law and security tools are weaponized against dissent while fentanyl and Venezuela are cast as national-security emergencies
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows emergency/terror frameworks used to bridge foreign confrontation and domestic policing.

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive Power Tests and Defies Institutional Checks at Home and Abroad
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the thread through Guard deployments, state-funding coercion, strikes, and institutional stress tests.

supporting_developments.development_title: Security forces and foreign policy are increasingly aligned with regime priorities and religious narratives
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds militarized domestic protest response, covert and overt strikes, and ideological framing of security actions.

aliases: domestic and foreign force with weak oversight
inclusion_notes: Include military deployments, war-powers reinterpretation, Guard federalization or deployment, security emergencies, terrorism framing used to expand executive force, and militarized protest policing.
Include foreign and domestic force in the same thread when they reflect the same weakly checked executive security logic.
exclusion_notes: Do not include routine immigration enforcement unless the key feature is military/security escalation rather than status control.
Do not include generic lawfare unless coercive force or security institutions are central.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_IMMIGRATION_AS_DOMESTIC_CONTROL, though the threads overlap when immigration enforcement becomes military-style.
Distinct from cand_RULE_BY_LAW_AND_ALLY_IMPUNITY, which concerns legal asymmetry more than force deployment.
Related to cand_SUPPRESSION_OF_DISSENT_AND_OPPOSITION, since security powers are often used to intimidate protest and opposition.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with labels around war powers, domestic militarization, national-security emergency governance, or coercive security-state expansion.
split_suggestions: Could split into foreign war powers and domestic militarization if later windows show they diverge significantly.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony capitalism and Saudi ties fuse foreign policy with Trump’s private business

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive power stretches past traditional limits through sweeping orders and emergency claims

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony capitalism and foreign-linked diplomacy fuse state policy with Trump-family business
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows industrial policy, diplomacy, and financial regulation intertwined with Trump-family or associate business interests.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony capitalism, foreign capital, and AI policy fuse economic power with regime interests
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the thread into AI, media, tariffs, strategic tech, and foreign-backed capital tied to insiders.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony capitalism, conflicts of interest, and partisan funding reshape the political economy
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows insider-like trades, Trump Media deals, partisan grant logic, and cross-border Trump-linked projects as one political economy.

inclusion_notes: Include donor-linked projects, contracts, regulatory favors, business deals, foreign-linked enrichment, patronage through public authority, and policies clearly shaped by insider financial interests.
Include symbolic or prestige state resources when they function as vehicles of elite enrichment or patronage.

Do not automatically include every pardon here; legal impunity belongs in cand_RULE_BY_LAW_AND_ALLY_IMPUNITY unless the financial patronage link is central.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_ADMINISTRATIVE_STATE_CAPTURE, which focuses on bureaucratic control; this thread focuses on who materially benefits.
Distinct from cand_PERSONALIST_STATE_AND_SYMBOLIC_DOMINANCE, though projects like the ballroom can overlap materially and symbolically.
Window support weakens after week 48 as developments shift toward other emphases; continuity in later windows would need confirmation.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with labels about oligarchy, donor capture, foreign-linked enrichment, or pay-to-play government.
split_suggestions: Could split into 'domestic donor patronage' and 'foreign-policy/business entanglement' if later windows support separate year-long arcs.

supporting_developments.development_title: Shutdown weaponized to attack SNAP, hollow out CDC, and sideline Congress
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows agency hollowing and shutdown leverage being used to restructure public-health and welfare capacity.

supporting_developments.development_title: Opposition constrained and civil service politicized through procedural and personnel control
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds politicized appointments, threats to workers, and weakening of institutional independence.

supporting_developments.development_title: Administrative state capture: CFPB, FHFA, USDA, and EPA repurposed for partisan and corporate aims
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly names and details agency capture across welfare, finance, housing, and environmental institutions.

supporting_developments.development_title: Security and civil service institutions bent toward loyalty, patronage, and private contractors
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows FBI, DHS, FEMA, VA, and related institutions reoriented around loyalty, outsourcing, and weakened safeguards.

supporting_developments.development_title: Regulatory and scientific institutions are captured, defunded, or bent toward ideological agendas

supporting_developments.development_title: Agencies Repurposed to Favor Fossil Fuels, Ideology, and Insiders over Public Goods

exclusion_notes: Do not fold all cronyism here unless the main story is about agency mission distortion rather than beneficiary enrichment.

Distinct from cand_INFO_CONTROL_AND_PROPAGANDA, although science suppression and data erasure can overlap.
This thread is visible across the window but most concentrated in selected weeks rather than every week.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with labels around regulatory capture, bureaucratic sabotage, civil-service purge, or agency politicization.
split_suggestions: Could split into 'scientific/public-health capture' and 'security/civil-service loyalty capture' if later windows sustain both distinctly.

supporting_developments.development_title: A coordinated federal campaign formalizes second‑class status for transgender people
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Provides a concentrated example of identity-based degradation across military, healthcare, housing, prisons, data, and education.

supporting_developments.development_title: Culture-war governance targets schools, libraries, and universities
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows state and federal policing of identities and support for marginalized groups in education and culture.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law and courts are weaponized against reproductive rights and marginalized groups amid patchy judicial pushback
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the thread to reproductive autonomy and ideologically stratified access to law and care.

exclusion_notes: Do not fold the entire immigration-enforcement apparatus here unless the emphasis is on status hierarchy rather than enforcement machinery.
Do not include generic culture-war rhetoric without concrete policy or institutional effects.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_IMMIGRATION_AS_DOMESTIC_CONTROL, which centers coercive machinery; this thread centers identity-based hierarchy across domains.

More normatively cross-domain than agency-specific candidate labels.
merge_suggestions: May merge with labels around second-class citizenship, anti-trans governance, reproductive coercion, or identity-based exclusion.
split_suggestions: Could split into 'anti-trans/LGBTQ governance' and 'reproductive-rights repression' if later windows support separate continuity.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Public institutions, symbols, and state identity reshaped around Trump’s persona and movement
candidate_threads.description: A recurring thread in which public spaces, federal institutions, commemorative practices, cultural bodies, and official symbolism are repurposed to glorify Trump, personalize state power, or redefine national identity around loyalty to a leader and movement rather than neutral civic institutions.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony capitalism and pay‑to‑play justice intertwine state power with Trump family and donor wealth
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Includes the East Wing demolition and donor-funded ballroom as an early symbolic and physical remaking of the White House around personal rule.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony capitalism and Saudi ties fuse foreign policy with Trump’s private business
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Touches the prestige-project dimension of state symbolism, though enrichment is the main focus.

supporting_developments.development_title: Public space, the White House, and religion are leveraged for symbolic dominance
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly centers architecture, park-pass imagery, and symbolic struggles over federal and religious space.

supporting_developments.development_title: Memory, media, and cultural institutions are reshaped to glorify Trump and mute scrutiny
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows altered presidential displays, renaming efforts, triumphal imagery, and term-limit trial balloons as leader-centric symbolic politics.

supporting_developments.development_title: Personalization of the State and Politicization of the Civil Service
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Combines civil-service hollowing with Trump-branded battleships, contested renamings, and movement-defined state identity.

supporting_developments.development_title: Federal power and public assets are wielded to punish disfavored regions and repurpose institutions for Trump’s glorification
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the pattern through Kennedy Center changes, public asset control, and punishment/reward through federal institutional symbolism.

inclusion_notes: Include renaming fights, symbolic architecture, public-branding moves, official iconography, and efforts to make institutions visibly serve a leader’s image or legacy.
Include personalization of public assets when the symbolic function is central, not merely financial benefit.
exclusion_notes: Do not include ordinary patronage or cronyism unless symbolism or personal glorification is a core feature.
Do not include all media propaganda here unless it is specifically leader-centric branding or memory politics.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_CRONYISM_AND_PRIVATE_STATE_FUSION, though the same project may carry both enrichment and symbolic-personalist meanings.
Distinct from cand_INFO_CONTROL_AND_PROPAGANDA, which is broader about narrative control; this thread is specifically about leader-centered state symbolism.
Potentially a sub-thread under a broader personalist-authoritarian umbrella if later windows justify it.
merge_suggestions: Could merge with labels around cult of personality, state symbolism, public-space branding, or personal rule aesthetics.
split_suggestions: If later windows support it, separate 'institutional/policy personalization' from 'symbolic/architectural glorification'.

notes_on_window: This window shows exceptionally strong continuity in immigration-as-control, law weaponization, information control, and militarized governance across nearly every week.
Several week-specific developments converge around elite accountability and the Epstein files; this is recurring enough within the window to preserve as a sub-thread even if it may later fold upward.
Economic-policy material divides into two more coherent continuity candidates: insider-enrichment/private-state fusion and agency capture. Generic 'economy' was avoided.

Resistance/civil-society appears in many weeks but more often as a counterpoint than as the primary governing method; it was not elevated to a top candidate thread here except indirectly in boundary notes.
