rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Strong in weeks 41-43 but fades after the shutdown ends; too period-bound for a window-level continuity thread spanning the full window.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.label: Economic pain and tariff disinformation
rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Too mixed between policy consequences and narrative spin; folded into broader info-control and cronyism/private-state fusion candidates.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.label: Culture-war governance in schools and universities
rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Real pattern but window evidence is better captured as part of stratified-rights and dissent-suppression threads than as a standalone continuity candidate.

Include cases where immigration enforcement is used to pressure states, cities, schools, hospitals, or protest spaces.

notes_on_window: This window strongly supports several sustained threads rather than one-off topic clusters, especially immigration as coercive domestic control, information control, weaponized law, and emergency/security power expansion.

Weeks 51-53 intensify and concretize earlier immigration and federal-retaliation patterns through the Minnesota surge, suggesting a useful later sub-thread or exemplar case but not necessarily a separate top-level continuity thread.

The Epstein files confrontation is unusually persistent across this window and useful to preserve as a sub-thread for later consolidation, even though it likely nests under broader rule-of-law and information-control categories.
Economic-pain and tariff narratives recur but are less coherent in this window as democratic-erosion methods than cronyism/private-state fusion and selective institutional capture.

Resistance appears frequently, but mostly as context or counterpressure rather than as a core erosion thread; it is better treated as cross-cutting context for later phases unless a year-wide resistance taxonomy is separately desired.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.label: Minnesota ICE surge as standalone top-level thread
rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Strongly recurring in the later half of the window, but best treated here as a vivid sub-case of immigration-as-control and punitive federalism unless it persists independently across multiple windows.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.label: Courts as uneven check
rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Important recurring context, but this is more an institutional response pattern than a governing method of erosion; better tracked in later status phases or folded into boundary/context notes.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.label: Tariff-driven economic pain
rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Present in several weeks but too topic-like and less coherent as a democratic-erosion method in this window than cronyism, administrative capture, or information manipulation.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.label: Culture-war governance in schools and libraries
rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Real pattern, but in this window it is better absorbed into the broader rights-rollback and information/memory-control threads rather than stand alone.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.label: Venezuela as standalone thread
rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Visible and intense in weeks 51-53, but analytically split across emergency powers, private enrichment, and information manipulation; too narrow as a separate continuity thread for this window.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.label: Civil society resistance and walkouts
rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Recurring and important, but it tracks opposition response rather than a governing erosion method and is therefore not prioritized in this discovery pass.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Substantive but window-limited; better folded into administrative/regulatory capture and targeted public-health rollback unless it recurs much more broadly in other windows.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Useful but narrower than the broader information/memory-control pattern and not independently strong enough for a top-level thread.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Immigration and citizenship are used as instruments of domestic control and tiered belonging
candidate_threads.description: A sustained pattern in which immigration enforcement, asylum restrictions, denaturalization threats, raids, detention buildouts, and nationality-targeted policies are used not just for border control but to create a rights-stratified political order and intimidate disfavored communities and jurisdictions.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration and citizenship become central tools of social control
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Explicitly frames immigration status, denaturalization threats, detention, and deportation as a system for stratifying rights by origin and ideology.

supporting_developments.development_title: From rhetoric to regime: a racialized immigration crackdown and tiered citizenship
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows the combination of dehumanizing rhetoric, asylum pauses, travel restrictions, raids, and nationality-focused enforcement into a tiered citizenship regime.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration enforcement hardens into a militarized, two-tier system
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Describes deportation infrastructure, Somali- and Afghan-focused crackdowns, and quasi-military enforcement as a durable governing system.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration enforcement hardens into a racialized, quasi-military regime
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Ties Supreme Court permission structure, racial profiling, raids, child coercion, and travel-ban logic into a more entrenched enforcement regime.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration Enforcement Expands into a Militarized, Dehumanizing Apparatus
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Highlights detention expansion, warehouse facilities, foreign-prison deportations, Guard deployments, and celebratory deportation messaging.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigration enforcement is industrialized and personalized under Trump
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows denaturalization quotas, country-based pauses, detention infrastructure, and Trump claiming personal control over coercive immigration tools.

supporting_developments.development_title: ICE Surge in Minnesota: From Targeted Crackdown to National Crisis Over State Violence
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Demonstrates how immigration enforcement becomes concentrated internal security pressure on a targeted community and city.

supporting_developments.development_title: Minnesota ICE Surge Becomes a De Facto Federal Occupation and Sparks Multi-Front Backlash
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows immigration enforcement functioning as quasi-occupation, with mass detentions, lethal force, and backlash from states and civil society.

supporting_developments.development_title: Minnesota becomes ground zero for a weaponized federal immigration crackdown
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Continues the pattern with mass ICE deployments, warrantless raids, child detentions, and political punishment of a blue-state jurisdiction.

aliases: immigration and citizenship as social control
inclusion_notes: Include denaturalization threats, nationality-targeted restrictions, detention and deportation buildout, and use of immigration enforcement against local communities or states.
Include cases where citizens, long-term residents, children, or protesters are swept into immigration-policing logic.
Include both policy-level changes and on-the-ground enforcement when they form one coercive system.
exclusion_notes: Exclude broader protest-policing or military-force stories unless immigration enforcement is central.
Exclude stand-alone foreign-policy migration diplomacy unless tied to domestic control or status stratification.

Distinct from cand_ANTI_DISSENT_AND_POLITICAL_INTIMIDATION, though immigration enforcement often overlaps when activists, journalists, or blue-state officials are targeted.
Could later contain a narrower Minnesota-focused sub-thread if other windows show it as a discrete episodic spike within the larger immigration-control pattern.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with candidates named 'immigration as social control', 'tiered citizenship', or 'deportation state buildout' from adjacent windows.
split_suggestions: If later windows sustain it, split off a sub-thread for 'Minnesota/blue-state occupation model' or 'denaturalization and citizenship stripping' as narrower recurring patterns.

Epstein-related opacity may be either this thread or information-control depending on whether the emphasis is impunity/DOJ shielding or narrative curation.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with 'rule by law', 'law as protection for allies and punishment for enemies', or 'selective justice' candidates elsewhere.
split_suggestions: If useful later, split a sub-thread on 'clemency and impunity for loyalists' from a sub-thread on 'investigative targeting of critics'.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Information, media, archives, and public memory are manipulated to protect the regime and shape reality
candidate_threads.description: A sustained pattern of controlling or distorting what the public can know through media intimidation, data suppression, curated disclosures, propaganda, archival manipulation, AI or visual disinformation, and leader-centered reshaping of civic memory.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information, media, and memory are aggressively curated to favor the regime
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Sets out suppression of data and science, broadcaster threats, book purges, and curated national memory as a coherent regime-favoring information strategy.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information warfare, managed opacity, and the curation of memory
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Adds media enemies lists, hidden economic indicators, politicized science, and selective transparency battles.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information systems and media are retooled for propaganda, speculation, and leader-centric branding
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows embedded speculation in news, media consolidation, propaganda branding, and leader-centered symbolic politics.

supporting_developments.development_title: Memory, media, and cultural institutions are reshaped to glorify Trump and mute scrutiny
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Connects lawsuits and settlements pressuring media with renaming, portrait politics, third-term signaling, and cultural-memory curation.

supporting_developments.development_title: Media Intimidation, Self-Censorship, and the Weaponization of Official Communications
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Centers assaults on journalists, outlet self-censorship, official smear messaging, and conspiracy amplification.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information control, disinformation, and the Epstein files fight reshape what the public is allowed to know
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Combines censorship, anti-disinformation retaliation, official falsehoods, and slow-walked disclosure in one information-control pattern.

supporting_developments.development_title: Narrative Warfare Around Minneapolis and January 6: Dissent Branded Terrorism, Insurrection Recast as Patriotism
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows selective footage, victim-smearing, and historical revisionism as active state narrative warfare.

supporting_developments.development_title: Smear Campaign and Information Control Around Renee Good and ICE Violence
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows coordinated disinformation, selective leaks, terrorist labeling, and journalist intimidation around state violence.

supporting_developments.development_title: Information control intensifies through AI manipulation, data misuse, and attacks on independent media
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the pattern to AI image manipulation, misuse of administrative data, election lies, and attacks on independent media and historical exhibits.

inclusion_notes: Include press intimidation, altered or withheld data, propaganda sites, selective leaks, archives/transparency manipulation, image or AI falsification, and cultural-symbol reshaping when aimed at narrative control.
Include politicization of public-health or economic information when the core issue is control of public knowledge.
exclusion_notes: Exclude legal-opacity cases when the central issue is prosecutorial impunity rather than narrative control.
Exclude ordinary culture-war policy unless memory, media, or public-information systems are central.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_WEAPONIZED_LAW_AND_SELECTIVE_JUSTICE, though DOJ stonewalling can support both threads.
Distinct from cand_CRONYISM_AND_PRIVATE_STATE_FUSION, even when media ownership or tech firms are part of the mechanism.
Book bans, school-library purges, and symbolic rebranding may sit on the boundary with culture-war governance; keep them here when memory curation or information restriction is the main pattern.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with 'information control and record erasure', 'propaganda and media intimidation', or 'managed opacity' labels from other windows.
split_suggestions: Possible future split between 'media intimidation/disinformation' and 'archives/memory/cultural-symbol control' if both become independently strong across the year.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: State power is fused with private enrichment, loyalist business networks, and patronage
candidate_threads.description: A recurring pattern in which economic policy, diplomacy, clemency, regulation, state assets, and public institutions are directed toward benefiting Trump-linked ventures, loyalist firms, politically connected financiers, or donor-aligned sectors, blurring governance and private gain.

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive power stretches past traditional limits through sweeping orders and emergency claims
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows emergency-style unilateralism used to entrench ideological and crony priorities in energy and infrastructure.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony capitalism and foreign-linked diplomacy fuse state policy with Trump-family business
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly links industrial policy, diplomacy, foreign fee streams, and Trump-family business interests.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony capitalism, foreign capital, and AI policy fuse economic power with regime interests
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows AI, trade, media, and foreign capital decisions shaped by insiders and sovereign-fund ties.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony capitalism, conflicts of interest, and partisan funding reshape the political economy
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Highlights insider trades, Trump-linked mergers, partisan grants, and economic narratives bent around private and partisan interest.

supporting_developments.development_title: Agencies Repurposed to Favor Fossil Fuels, Ideology, and Insiders over Public Goods
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows agencies redirected toward fossil-fuel, crypto, and insider-aligned outcomes at the expense of neutral public goods.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony Capitalism in Venezuela and at Home: Oil, Crypto, and Militarized Budgets
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Connects foreign intervention, oil deals, crypto ventures, and militarized budgeting to insider enrichment.

supporting_developments.development_title: Executive Economic Power: Venezuelan Oil, Global Tariffs, and Health-Care Leverage
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows executive economic levers used in donor-linked or insider-benefiting ways, especially around Venezuelan oil flows.

supporting_developments.development_title: Crony crypto capitalism: law and regulation are bent to favor Trump-linked financial interests
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Concentrates the pattern in crypto deregulation, clemency, patronage appointments, and market rules tailored to Trump-linked interests.

inclusion_notes: Include cases where state policy, diplomatic action, regulatory choices, clemency, or public assets materially advantage Trump-linked firms, donors, family ventures, or aligned industries.
Include foreign-linked deals when they illuminate the same patronage logic.
exclusion_notes: Exclude general deregulatory ideology unless there is a clear insider-benefit or patronage dimension.
Exclude leader symbolism without a material patronage or asset-allocation component.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_WEAPONIZED_LAW_AND_SELECTIVE_JUSTICE, though pardons and dropped probes may serve both patronage and selective-justice logics.
Distinct from cand_SECURITY_FORCES_AND_EMERGENCY_POWER even where foreign intervention yields economic spoils; keep those here only when private enrichment is central.
Can overlap with personalization of the state, but this candidate focuses on material benefit and patronage rather than symbolic glorification.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with 'crony capitalism', 'state-business fusion', or 'patronage and oligarchic governance' candidates from other windows.
split_suggestions: Possible later split between 'foreign-policy/oil/crypto self-dealing' and 'domestic agency capture for donor sectors' if needed.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Dissent, protest, journalism, and political opposition are treated as threats to be intimidated or criminalized
candidate_threads.description: A recurring pattern in which protesters, journalists, lawmakers, oversight voices, and disfavored communities are smeared, investigated, raided, disciplined, or physically endangered so that opposition appears subversive, criminal, or unsafe.

supporting_developments.development_title: Security forces and quasi-paramilitary tactics are turned inward to intimidate communities and lawmakers
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows masked street snatches, raids, swatting, and fear-based pressure on communities and officials.

supporting_developments.development_title: Protest and dissent squeezed by immigration crackdowns, policing tactics, and targeted investigations
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Directly treats protest and opposition as security problems managed through raids, force, and scrutiny.

supporting_developments.development_title: Surveillance, intimidation, and rhetoric escalate against dissenters and marginalized communities
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Captures border questioning, detention over speech, and presidential attacks that stigmatize critics and minorities.

supporting_developments.development_title: Immigrant scapegoating and anti-dissent narratives are amplified through official propaganda and policing
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows propaganda and policing working together to cast targeted groups and anti-ICE activism as dangerous.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil Society Mobilizes Against Authoritarian Drift Amid Ongoing Rights Battles
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Provides the resistance side of a context where activism and pluralism require active defense against escalating authoritarian pressure.

supporting_developments.development_title: Legislatures and cultural bodies punish dissent and reframe oversight as disorder
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows censures, expulsions, punitive spectacle, and framing of protest and oversight as disorder to be controlled.

supporting_developments.development_title: Narrative Warfare Around Minneapolis and January 6: Dissent Branded Terrorism, Insurrection Recast as Patriotism
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows dissenters and victims cast as terrorists while loyalist violence is sanitized.

supporting_developments.development_title: Law as a Weapon: DOJ Targets Journalists and Lawmakers While Probing the Fed
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Captures raids on journalists and investigations of lawmakers for discussing illegal orders, demonstrating direct intimidation of oversight voices.

supporting_developments.development_title: Dissent and local opposition are branded as insurrection and corruption to justify harsher measures
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows rhetorical delegitimization of protesters and critics to justify punishment, primary challenges, and harsher state action.

inclusion_notes: Include raids, intimidation, threat rhetoric, protest policing, investigations of journalists or lawmakers, punitive legislative discipline, and official labeling of dissent as terrorism, corruption, or insurrection.
Include overlap with immigration enforcement when the point is suppression of protest or chilling of criticism.
exclusion_notes: Exclude broader immigration-control stories unless protest, speech, journalism, or political opposition is central.
Exclude general information warfare unless intimidation of critics is the main mechanism.
boundary_notes: Distinct from cand_IMMIGRATION_AS_CONTROL, though many intimidation episodes occur through ICE or border authorities.
Distinct from cand_INFO_CONTROL_AND_PROPAGANDA, which centers manipulation of public knowledge rather than coercion against dissenters themselves.
Distinct from cand_WEAPONIZED_LAW_AND_SELECTIVE_JUSTICE, though legal targeting is often one instrument within this broader anti-opposition pattern.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with labels like 'criminalization of dissent', 'opposition intimidation', or 'speech and protest repression' from other windows.
split_suggestions: Could later split between 'journalist/lawmaker intimidation' and 'street-level protest suppression' if those trajectories remain distinct.

candidate_threads.canonical_name: Courts, Congress, states, and civil society mount uneven but meaningful resistance to executive overreach
candidate_threads.description: A recurring counter-thread in which judges, legislatures, local governments, states, and organized civil society sometimes slow, expose, or partially block authoritarian moves—but do so inconsistently and often after the fact.

supporting_developments.development_title: Courts deliver mixed signals as some rulings check abuse while others entrench conservative power
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Introduces the core pattern of uneven judicial checking mixed with enabling decisions.

supporting_developments.development_title: Courts and Congress offer uneven resistance as judicial partisanship shapes outcomes
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows a tug-of-war in which some institutions constrain overreach while others entrench it.

supporting_developments.development_title: Institutions and civil society mount uneven but notable resistance
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Most explicit statement of mosaic resistance by courts, legislatures, and civic groups.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil rights narrow for immigrants and LGBTQ+ youth as some institutions still resist
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Provides examples of local elections, courts, and state action resisting exclusionary federal moves.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil Society Mobilizes Against Authoritarian Drift Amid Ongoing Rights Battles
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Shows public art, walkouts, and litigation as organized resistance to shrinking pluralism.

supporting_developments.development_title: Civil society and subnational actors mount targeted resistance on voting, war powers, climate, and education
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Demonstrates subnational and civil-society burden-sharing in defending democratic norms and public goods.

supporting_developments.development_title: Courts and States Offer Uneven but Real Checks on Federal Overreach
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Names and exemplifies the patchy but real judicial and state-level constraints on retaliation and abuse.

supporting_developments.development_title: Institutions push back unevenly as courts, Congress, and agencies test their limits
supporting_developments.why_it_supports_thread: Extends the resistance pattern into injunctions, hearings, forced resignations, and technocratic pockets of restraint.

inclusion_notes: Include court injunctions, oversight hearings, state protections, local countermeasures, and organized civic resistance when they function as checks on authoritarian actions.
Include mixed or contradictory institutional behavior when the key point is inconsistency of guardrails.
exclusion_notes: Exclude mere routine governance not meaningfully checking overreach.
Exclude resistance episodes that are too localized unless they clearly exemplify a recurring institutional pattern.
boundary_notes: This is a countervailing thread, not a pro-regime method; keep it because it recurs across many weeks and is central for later consolidation.
Distinct from cand_ANTI_DISSENT_AND_POLITICAL_INTIMIDATION, though many resistance episodes arise in response to that pressure.
Could later be split into institutional resistance versus civil-society resistance, but in this window they frequently appear as one mosaic.
merge_suggestions: Likely merge with 'uneven resistance', 'fragmented checks', or 'institutions and civil society push back' candidates from other windows.
split_suggestions: Possible future split into 'judicial/congressional checks' and 'grassroots/subnational resistance' if later windows support separate treatment.

notes_on_window: This window shows especially strong continuity around immigration enforcement as a governing method, not merely a policy area.
Minnesota emerges in weeks 51-53 as a concentrated theater within larger threads rather than a wholly separate top-level thread for this window.

Epstein-related developments recur strongly, but in this window they read more as a cross-cutting subpattern of selective justice and information control than as the best standalone top-level continuity thread.
Economic hardship and social-policy retrenchment recur, but the more durable continuity visible here is crony/private-state fusion rather than a broad 'economy' thread.

Culture-war governance appears repeatedly, especially around LGBTQ+, DEI, and education, but within this window it is often better treated as part of broader information control, anti-dissent, or tiered-belonging patterns rather than a separate top-level candidate.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Recurring and important, but within this window it functions mainly as a subpattern of selective justice and information/archives control rather than the strongest standalone continuity thread.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Visible in multiple weeks, but too interwoven here with information control, civil-rights rollback, and tiered belonging to stand alone cleanly at window level.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.label: Personalization of the state and leader glorification
rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Real recurring motif, but mostly better treated as a facet of information/memory control and crony patronage in this window.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Highly salient but too geographically specific as a top-level window candidate; best treated as a concentrated episode within immigration-as-control, anti-dissent, and security-power threads.

rejected_or_folded_candidates.reason: Multi-week pattern exists, but in this window it is less coherent as a democracy-method thread than adjacent patterns of civil-rights hierarchy and patronage governance.
